_notes: Stack patterns from Table 5 of the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria (potentially clinically important drug-drug interactions to avoid in older adults). Each pattern was checked against the published table on the date in its `verifiedOn` field; see docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md. This is a partial list and the wording is paraphrased. The drug groups refer to class lists in drug_classes.json. Rule types: "pair" fires when the stack has at least one drug from groupA and a different drug from groupB; "count" fires when at least minCount different drugs in the stack belong to any of the listed groups. An absent insight does not mean a stack is safe. Not medical advice.

sources: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. Full text read from PubMed Central (author manuscript): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12478568/
NLM RxNorm and RxClass (https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/) for brand-name ingredients and for membership of classes the paper names without listing drugs.
verification.rule: Matchers ignore any entry whose `verified` value is not "confirmed" or "corrected".

sources.beers-2023-table-5: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. Table 5.

patterns.label: Opioid with a benzodiazepine
patterns.reason: Increased risk of overdose and adverse events.
patterns.verificationNote: Follow-up re-read of the reason against the table row: the row says only "Increased risk of overdose and adverse events"; slowed breathing and sedation came from the Table 2 benzodiazepine row.

patterns.label: Opioid with gabapentin or pregabalin
patterns.reason: Taking an opioid with gabapentin or pregabalin increases the risk of severe sedation, slowed breathing and death.
patterns.recommendation: Avoid. Exceptions are when changing over from an opioid to gabapentin or pregabalin, or when using them to reduce the opioid dose, although caution is needed in all cases.

patterns.label: Two or more strongly anticholinergic medicines
patterns.reason: Using more than one anticholinergic medicine increases the risk of cognitive decline, delirium, and falls or fractures.
patterns.recommendation: Avoid. Keep the number of anticholinergic medicines to a minimum.

patterns.label: Three or more medicines that act on the central nervous system
patterns.reason: Taking three or more of these medicines together (antiepileptics including gabapentin and pregabalin, antidepressants, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, Z-drug sleep medicines, opioids and skeletal muscle relaxants) increases the risk of falls and fractures.
patterns.recommendation: Avoid taking three or more at the same time. Keep the number of these medicines to a minimum.
patterns.verifiedAgainst: Table 5, row "Any combination of 3 or more of these CNS-active drugs"
patterns.verificationNote: The seven drug types match the table row exactly. Follow-up: gabapentin and pregabalin are now cited through the separate gabapentinoids list, because the table row says "Antiepileptics (including gabapentinoids)". Behaviour is unchanged.

patterns.label: Lithium with an ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI
patterns.recommendation: Avoid. If used together, lithium levels should be monitored.
patterns.verificationNote: Follow-up re-read of the reason against the table row: the row says only "Increased risk of lithium toxicity"; the statement that these medicines raise lithium levels was not in it.

patterns.label: Lithium with a loop diuretic
patterns.recommendation: Avoid. If used together, lithium levels should be monitored.
patterns.verificationNote: Follow-up re-read of the reason against the table row: the row says only "Increased risk of lithium toxicity"; the statement that these medicines raise lithium levels was not in it.

patterns.label: Warfarin with amiodarone
patterns.recommendation: Avoid when possible. If used together, the INR should be monitored closely.
patterns.verificationNote: Follow-up re-read of the reason against the table row: the row says only "Increased risk of bleeding"; the statement about increasing the effect of warfarin was not in it.

patterns.recommendation: Avoid when possible. If used together, the INR should be monitored closely.
